title: Draft Integrated Multi-Paragraph Text
outcome: Write a reader-focused formal request Draft V1 with all required information and distinct functional paragraph jobs; retain the very first saved draft for later revision.

lessons: A draft is a message to a real reader, not a list of connectors. Map required facts and polite action first.
Planning is a route, not a cage. A requirement must appear somewhere, but two, three or four coherent paragraphs may work.

demo.prompt: Write a polite email to a community museum manager suggesting one beginner map-making workshop. Propose a possible time, a simple activity and ask for consideration; do not assert museum approval.
steps: Reader museum manager; request to consider; tentative timing, activity and clear decision request.
P1 purpose/proposal; P2 timing/activity; P3 courteous question and thanks.

Dear Museum Manager, I am writing to ask whether the museum could consider a beginner map-making workshop for local students. One possible time is a Saturday afternoon. Participants could draw a simple map of a familiar area and compare roads and landmarks. Would you consider this idea or suggest a suitable alternative? Thank you for your time. Kind regards, Alex.
Each paragraph has a reader job; no event approval is claimed.
The claim 'Map workshops are fantastic' does not supply a time or activity.
Check every task requirement against actual draft sentences, not a connector/word count.

teaching.a1: I am writing to ask if … / One possible activity is … / Thank you for considering …
teaching.b1: Suggest a small-group or supply constraint as a possibility, not an established policy.

cycleA.prompt: Email a neighbourhood sports hall manager asking them to consider a trial after-school table-tennis session. Include one suggested weekday, registration suggestion, one resource to check and polite decision request. Treat all as proposals, not an approved event.

taskStrip.task: Ask the sports hall manager to consider a trial
taskStrip.mustInclude: Weekday; registration; resource check; decision request
taskStrip.boundary: Provisional plan, manager audience, no invented approval or attendance

cards.text: Could the hall consider a trial table-tennis session on a Wednesday after school?
cards.rationale: Names the proposal and tentative day.

cards.text: Interested students could sign up through the hall desk, if that option is available.
cards.rationale: Proposed registration, not a confirmed arrangement.

cards.text: The hall would also need to check whether tables are available.
cards.rationale: A resource check, no invented inventory.

cards.text: Please let us know whether the idea could work. Thank you for considering it.
The trial is officially approved and starts tomorrow.
cards.rationale: The task is still provisional; approval is invented.

cards.text: My aunt watches football on television.

labels.text: A polite request for manager's decision

cycleA.falseOpening: Dear Manager, table tennis is good. We are sure the trial is already approved.

ownFields.label: Your rewrite: remove false approval and make a polite request
Why does your revision preserve the uncertain/proposal status?

cycleB.prompt: First-time visitors to a community arts centre may not know how to join weekend workshops. Write a polite email to the programme coordinator proposing clearer sign-up instructions. Include where and when to register, what participants should bring, one concrete benefit, and ask for consideration. Do NOT invent current registration policies.

taskStrip.task: Polite request to programme coordinator for clearer first-time information
taskStrip.mustInclude: Visitors potentially confused; where/when registration; what to bring; one practical benefit; consideration request
taskStrip.boundary: No invented hours/policy/approval/numbers; 90–130 words only optional guidance

fields.label: Your 2–3 paragraph jobs — planning notes, not a complete draft

cycleB.a1: I am writing to ask if … / One possible activity is … / Thank you for considering …
cycleB.b1: Optional: qualify feasibility without claiming a known policy. Length guidance 90–130 words, never a score threshold.

transfer.prompt: Write a respectful email to a school committee asking it to consider a shaded waiting space for students after clubs. State when the need is noticeable, propose one feasible arrangement, explain one direct benefit and ask for consideration. Do not invent a budget or approved plan.

fields.label: Why does the closing ask the right reader to consider the proposal?

extras.prompt: Propose beginners' badminton afternoon by email; include a suggested date and first-time equipment.
extras.question: Which covers practical details?

options.text: Badminton is fun, fun and very fun.
Could the club consider a beginners' badminton afternoon next Saturday? New players could bring their own racket if available.
options.rationale: Tentative time, equipment and no invented approval.

options.text: The afternoon has already been approved and everyone must attend.

extras.prompt: Request an art display from school office: purpose, possible location, and polite decision.
extras.question: Which three-part plan has distinct jobs?

options.text: P1: art is great; P2: art is very great; P3: art is great again.
P1: your weekend; P2: unrelated films; P3: thank reader.
P1: ask for display; P2: possible location and benefit; P3: politely request a decision.
P1: everything in headline; P2/P3: empty.

extras.prompt: School has NOT decided about a Saturday language-help desk; student asks permission.
extras.question: Which keeps decision status accurate?

options.text: The help desk opens every Saturday, as officially agreed.
Everyone must use it this weekend.
The desk is guaranteed to improve every grade.
Could the school consider trying a Saturday language-help desk?

extras.prompt: Swimming club has NOT agreed to a proposed family information session.
extras.question: Which closing is appropriate?

options.text: Thank you for approving the session and paying for everything.
Would you consider this idea and let us know whether it may be possible? Thank you for your time.
I demand a guaranteed reply by tomorrow morning.

aiLens: Review exact saved Draft V1 and task strip only after explicit learner request. Prioritize grounded missing requirements, reader mismatch or concrete-detail weakness; accept strong work without manufacturing errors. No full replacement letter, grade, CEFR level or invented policy. Preserve first immutable Draft V1 for later U10/U11.
